title: Intel host capital productivity: primary evidence and owned prospective adjudication
scope: One additive research and policy recommendation; no engine edits, changed equity values, model grid or prior-arithmetic rerun. External packaging remains a separate funded program.
chronology: Earlier base, funded-CPU and packaging values were already known. No new equity output was computed or inspected during this capital-policy selection. The proposed0.80 and range were communicated to root before any valuation under them.

owned_decision.recommendation: Prefer0.80 incremental sales per dollar of total net operating reinvestment for the host from2031 onward; retain0.60–1.00 as a plausible planning range. This is an owned estimate, not an empirically fitted marginal-capital coefficient or a statistical confidence interval.
owned_decision.old_060_judgment: 0.60 is a defensible capital-heavy outcome, but the evidence is insufficient to make it the uniquely most likely mature requirement. It is not proved punitive: historical Intel flow comparisons can approach it when acquisitions and other cash needs are included, and future leading-edge tools remain expensive.
owned_decision.why_080: Intel has already paid for substantial shell/campus capacity, is deploying tools into existing fabs, and explicitly seeks longer-lived nodes and chiplet reuse. After paying the current ramp, I expect that repeatable model to improve productivity relative to the catch-up/build-ahead phase. A0.80 convention still funds1.25 dollars of net operating capital per dollar of additional annual sales; it does not assume a fabless model or free node transitions.
owned_decision.why_not_above_100: High-NA/EUV tools, greater U.S. production, qualification/startup cycles, supplier advances and uncertain external utilization prevent adopting the much lighter mature-node TI model or TSMC’s current AI-cycle flow productivity as Intel’s permanent outcome.
owned_decision.implementation_if_adopted: Replace only the host2031+ turnover schedule with0.80. Keep selected revenue/profits, D&A (reaching20% Products), WC10% of incremental host external sales,3% nominal maturity, corporate costs and all credit/claim policies unchanged. Capital=DA+delta host external sales/0.80−deltaWC. No automatic further margin or tax benefit. Packaging keeps its independently funded1.00 turnover; do not apply0.80 to it again.
owned_decision.confidence: More confident that0.60 is not well calibrated than that0.80 is precise. The plausible range remains economically material; it should limit conviction in either stock direction rather than be hidden.

definitions_and_scope.turnover: Incremental sales divided by capex minus total normalized D&A plus operating working-capital investment. It is a flow-reinvestment assumption, not annual sales divided by ending PP&E.
definitions_and_scope.gross_capex_vs_net_growth: D&A20% is not a second independent FCFF penalty when gross capex is DA plus net investment minusWC. Nevertheless, those depreciation and manufacturing-profit assumptions must describe economically plausible recurring tool costs. No mathematical double charge was found.
definitions_and_scope.nominal_scope: 3% nominal revenue growth need not be3% additional wafer starts. Price/mix and physical capacity both matter; net reinvestment can include replacement-cost inflation as well as new capacity. No exact real-capacity split is inferred.
definitions_and_scope.funding: Government incentives, minority funding and customer deposits alter who supplies cash and its timing; they are not themselves higher physical capital productivity. Existing finite subsidy and claim treatments remain separate.

same_company_evidence.finding: 2024 manufacturing capex including technology development was55% facility space and45% equipment. Intel described recent outsized spending on technology, shells and tools and delaying tools until demand confidence.
same_company_evidence.implication: Part of the past spend buys future space rather than current sales. Supports a utilization/tooling transition; does not make fitting out those shells or every later node free.

same_company_evidence.finding: Intel explicitly aims to lengthen node lifespans through optimization, older-node roles in disaggregated products and external use. NetPP&E105.414B includes34.543B CIP; grossPP&E211.878B is reduced by16.1B capital incentives. Incentives reduced2025 depreciation by1.0B.
same_company_evidence.implication: Reuse is a strategic basis for better productivity, while unfinished and subsidized book assets make current average turnover unsuitable as a direct marginal calibration. No assumption of unlimited external mature-node demand.

same_company_evidence.finding: Certain equipment lives increased from5to8years in January2023; estimated2023 depreciation reduction4.2B. The resulting expense/inventory effects were not individually quantifiable after cost absorption.
same_company_evidence.implication: A historical capex-minus-book-depreciation ratio moves when accounting life changes, even without a matching change in current physical additions. Longer accounting life alone is not proof of economic asset survival.

same_company_evidence.finding: Existing Ireland cleanrooms receive tools;18A-P reuses design infrastructure; Intel3/18A and packaging capacity continue to ramp. Equipment purchase orders and future capex also rise.
same_company_evidence.implication: The causal route is more qualified output from existing space plus paid new tools. Design-rule reuse does not establish a free or universally fungible fab. Current2027–30 investment is retained, not recouped or removed.

historical_flow_diagnostic.locators: Printedpage50 selectedfinancialdata (PDF52); cashflows printed77 (PDF79); PP&E printed87 (PDF89). Cashflow/PP&E tables visually checked.
historical_flow_diagnostic.WC_scope: AR, inventory,AP, accrued compensation and prepaid supply cashflow lines; excludes taxes and unclassified other assets/liabilities.
historical_flow_diagnostic.interpretation: Approx0.727 is a multiyear flow diagnostic, not a causal marginal return. Counting acquisition cash gives0.636, underscoring scope sensitivity. NAND, acquisitions/disposals, future-node development, noncash capital/payables, capitalized interest and the pre-EUV process mix prevent treating either number as the forecast coefficient. It restrains an aggressive productivity upgrade while showing0.60 is not the only observed scale.

TSMC.implication: 2025capex/revenue33.4% andDA/revenue18.1%;41.1% of netPP&E was equipment-under-installation/CIP. In OctoberTSMC reiterated60–64BUSD2026capex and heavier2026–28investment while discussing tool costs and overseas dilution. This supports a substantial recurring leading-edge burden, not a direct0.60 coefficient. Wafer-service revenue differs from Intel’s product revenue, growth rates differ, and installed capital serves later demand.
TSMC.verification: Annual figures reviewed by delegated primary-source researcher; October issuer-hosted transcript independently opened by hardware researcher.

TI.finding: Management described a roughly4% revenue no-growth gross-capex floor and a Phase3 modular-expansion relationship near1.2 times long-term revenue growth for grosscapex/revenue, before incentives.
TI.implication: This is an explicit economic spending relationship rather than average book turnover, demonstrating why a prebuilt-shell phase can mature into more flexible investment. TI’s28–130nm, long-lived analog/embedded products and equipment do not calibrate Intel’s continuing leading-edge logic program; do not substitute its4% replacement floor.
TI.verification: Primary web text read by delegated researcher. Hardware’s independent refetch returned403; no local transcript retained and no claim of visual verification.

comparables_scope_review.funding_guard: Peer grants reduce recorded asset basis and depreciation; customer capacity deposits may be repayable or offset shipments. Neither is free physical capacity or a permanent cost reduction. No peer subsidy/financing credit is added to Intel.

mature_operating_sanity_only.source: Existing fundedCPU host2041operating row; no equity output
mature_operating_sanity_only.interpretation: At3% nominal growth and unchanged20%-of-Products D&A,0.80 still produces roughly22.95% grosscapex/host external sales, versus24.17% under0.60. Maintenance/replacement and new growth remain funded. Historical/peer ratios are scope checks, not coefficients selected by averaging.

counterfacts_and_update_criteria: Favor0.60orlower productivity if successor-node tooling/qualification spend remains catch-up-like despite current shell spending, old nodes lose internal/external demand, or geographical duplication persistently raises capital per accepted output.

Favor1.00orhigher if publicly disclosed qualified wafer/package output and retained node demand rise on sustained lower tool/site additions across multiple years, without outsourcing cost simply replacing capital or subsidized asset funding being counted as productivity.

Review aggregate capital and accepted product/service output together. Do not change the coefficient because an isolated quarter’s capex or cash depreciation moved, or because a stock value needs a different answer.

separate_CPU_host_update.owned_preference: Prefer20% Intel2027unit growth as central and retain30% as a funded upside. Ireland output doubling is not all-company CPU doubling. This demand preference is independent of the0.80 capital proposal and is not a compensating price-fitting adjustment.
separate_CPU_host_update.scope: This is an independent analyst forecast, not an observed physical ceiling or actual future Intel market share. No model changed here.
